title: Prefetch Credit Ledger — client-side accounting & reconciliation (journal)
content:
Context and motivation:

This is a personal design journal exploring a lightweight, client-first ledger for prefetch credits that can be reconciled by the runtime. Objective: avoid overcharging customers, allow safe optimistic prefetching on clients, support partial offload/handoff when sessions move between devices or to server, and keep telemetry small.

Design goals (high level):
- Cheap on-client bookkeeping (small footprint, O(1) per-prefetch)
- Deterministic reconciliation rules so server can deterministically verify client claims when provided with a sparse audit log
- Bounded staleness: ledger entries expire after TTL or when reconciled
- Support transfer/merge of ledger from one client to another (handoff) without double-consuming credits
- Minimal synchronous round trips for allocation (optimistic local allocation with later server validation)

Terminology:
- credit: an atomic unit representing budgeted token-prefetch capacity (not equal to tokens; conservative mapping configurable)
- prefetch: client-initiated request to preheat KV/prefix/context tokens for a session
- ledger: append-only sequence of local operations (allocate, consume, refund, transfer) with monotonic local index and short-lived signature (HMAC)

Core idea: optimistic allocations + compact audit receipts
1) Client can allocate N credits locally using local_counter++ and emit a ledger entry: ALLOC(n, seq, hint). This buys the client permission to prefetch up to n units without blocking.
2) Server exposes an async verification endpoint where it ingests compact receipts (batchable) and replies with a compact signed acknowledgement that a subset of the allocations are accepted.
3) If the server rejects or reduces allocations, client reconciles (refunds returned to pool) and may backoff.

Ledger schema (flat text format used in client storage):
- entries are newline separated small records: TS | SEQ | OP | N | SESSION_HINT | HMAC
- example: 1700000000|12|ALLOC|5|ctx=doc-123|hmac:abcd...
- ops: ALLOC, CONSUME, REFUND, TRANSFER_OUT, TRANSFER_IN, EXPIRE

API sketch (compact; optimistic path):
- POST /v1/prefetch/allocations/batch
  body: [ {"session_id":"s1","seq":12,"op":"ALLOC","n":5,"hint":"doc-123","ts":1700000000,"hmac":"..."}, ... ]
  response: {"acks": [ {"seq":12,"accepted":5,"server_token":"t_k2"}, ... ] }

- POST /v1/prefetch/reconcile
  body: {"session_id":"s1","ledger_head":24}
  response: {"status":"ok","balance_delta":-3,"notes":"adjusted down due to quota"}

Server-side verification rules (notes):
- HMAC is derived from a per-client ephemeral key handed out at session start (short TTL). This prevents arbitrary forgery but keeps server stateless between verification batches if it persists ephemeral keys for recon windows.
- Deterministic validation: server replays ledger ops in increasing seq order per session; any gaps mark potential out-of-order handing and cause temporary hold/backoff.
- Idempotency: server stores only per-session confirmed counters (confirmed_allocations, confirmed_consumes) and dedup by seq/HMAC. Keeps DB footprint small.

Reconciliation heuristics:
- Soft-rejection: if server has insufficient budget, it accepts part of ALLOC (accepted < requested) and returns refund info. Client immediately emits a REFUND entry and reduces local pool.
- Stale-merge: when two clients merge ledgers (TRANSFER_IN/TRANSFER_OUT), server requires both sides include overlapping proof frames (a small signed snapshot) to avoid double-spend. Transfer flow: transferer writes TRANSFER_OUT(seq_x, n, target_id) -> transferee writes TRANSFER_IN(seq_y, n, source_id) -> submit both to reconcile endpoint in same batch.
- Expiry: server enforces max TTL (configurable, default 24h). After TTL, any unacknowledged ALLOC is considered EXPIRE and reclaimed on reconcile. Client emits EXPIRE entries as housekeeping.

Telemetry and billing mapping:
- Keep telemetry coarse: counts of alloc/consume/refund per route/model and a 95pct latency histogram for allocation ack. Do not send entire ledger to telemetry.
- Billing decision rule: only server-acknowledged CONSUMEs or ALLOCs accepted by server are billable. Optimistic local allocations are NOT billed until server ack. This protects customers and requires server to process reconcile batches in a timely fashion.

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Client offline > TTL: client-held allocations expire. When client reconnects, server will reject and client must refresh. UX: show a brief "prefetch warmup failed" fallback and gracefully degrade.
- Partial batch loss: client should keep local ledger until it gets explicit server ack for each seq; retry with exponential backoff with jitter. Ledger retention default 72h to allow for delayed reconciliation.
- Clock skew: use monotonic local seq and server-side timestamping; server should accept client TS but authoritative ordering uses seq.

ASCII sequence diagram (transfer example):
ClientA         Server            ClientB
   |             |                   |
   | TRANSFER_OUT(seq=50,n=10,target=B) |
   |------------> store pending -------->|
   |             |<-- hold until B ok --|
   |             |                   |
   |             |<<-- submit both -> reconcile endpoint
   |             | process, issue ACKs  |
   |<--- ACK(transfer confirmed) ------|

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to handle cross-tenant transfers? (probably disallow unless same tenant)
- Ephemeral key rotation window sizing: tradeoff between security and re-sync cost (15m vs 2h)
- Exact billing unit mapping: credits->tokens ratio should be workload-configurable and surfaced in Console
- Impact on server-side DB write amplification with many small reconcile batches; need batching heuristics (threshold time N ops or bytes).

Immediate next steps (for a prototype):
- implement minimal client ledger lib (JS + small C shim) that supports append/read/persist + compact batch builder
- wire server batch endpoint with deterministic verification and simple in-memory confirmed counters (feature flag behind dev env)
- test transfer flow across devices using local emulator and verify idempotency and no-double-spend

Notes to self: keep ledger format intentionally simple so it can be snuck into existing session blobs. Avoid long lived cryptographic keys in client; prefer ephemeral HMAC with occasional revalidation via a short token exchange.

References / links to existing thinking:
- see GH issue for optimistic prefetch allocation: GH:repo/inference-runtime/issues/742
- prefetch backpressure notes (related): slack:#ingress-telemetry thread ts=1708000000

End of journal entry (still rough).
